subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden `NO_REPLY` handling to suppress otherwise substantive text before a trailing or own-line sentinel, or keep the current mixed-content-preserving behavior except for narrower reasoning/silent-intent and token-only cases?
rationale: Current main and the latest release intentionally preserve ordinary substantive text before trailing `NO_REPLY`, while the reported leak class is security-sensitive; automation cannot choose the privacy-versus-message-delivery boundary without maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Adopt a narrow shared classifier
options.body: Suppress reasoning, silent-intent, and internal-summary payloads consistently across delivery paths while preserving ordinary substantive replies that only mention or accidentally end with `NO_REPLY`.

options.title: Suppress any trailing sentinel payload
options.body: Treat any trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` as whole-payload silence, accepting possible loss of legitimate replies that current tests preserve.

options.title: Keep current semantics
options.body: Leave the generic mixed-content behavior unchanged and close or retitle this issue to the already-merged narrower leak classes.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow shared classifier
recommendation.body: Suppress reasoning, silent-intent, and internal-summary payloads consistently across delivery paths while preserving ordinary substantive replies that only mention or accidentally end with `NO_REPLY`.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the recent overlapping token-classifier fixes and is the clearest routing owner for the remaining policy boundary.
